sources: dossier=Required behaviors ('Every handler runs inside a short fresh transaction; no handler in this surface mutates state.', 2026-05-11 log-convergence, artifact-only, sole source); doc=cascade-graph.md:24 (pre-fix) 'All cascade-graph HTTP handlers run inside a short fresh transaction'; code=handler.go handleListClaimProducers/handleListExecutors/handleGetExecutor read only deps.Discovery (in-memory cache, no Tables call); handleListNodeRuns/handleGetNodeRun/handleSystemSummary read deps.Queue (a separate interface from Tables) with no Tables.Transaction wrapper
note: The read-only half of the dossier's claim holds and stays; the 'every handler' transaction-scoping half is structurally unsatisfiable for cache- and queue-backed handlers (they touch no table, so there is nothing to wrap in a Tables transaction) and the current handler set includes several such handlers. Narrowed the invariant to state which handlers open a table transaction and which read a non-table source directly, preserving the dossier's core intent (short-lived, read-only access) without the unfalsifiable blanket claim.

sources: dossier=Net position ('Routes are mounted at bare paths with no /v1/ prefix, matching control-api versioning discipline', 2026-05-11 log-convergence, artifact-only, sole source); doc=cascade-graph.md:26 'mounted under the control API's versioned prefix, matching the parent control-api versioning discipline' vs control-api.md:25 'The operation surface is unversioned at the wire'; code=app.go:80 r.Route("/v1", ...) wraps every route including /v1/observability/*, with no bare-path route registered anywhere
note: Design-call: the dossier's own 'bare paths, no /v1/ prefix' claim is directly falsified by the code (100% of routes, including observability, are literally under /v1), so it cannot ground a confident fix-doc ruling on its own (suspect-canonization — artifact-only, single-source, and contradicted by observed structure). But it's not simply refutable either, because 'unversioned at the wire' in control-api.md is genuinely ambiguous: it could mean 'no rolling version scheme, though a fixed /v1 literal exists forever' (compatible with the current doc text and code) or 'no version segment should exist in the path at all' (matching the dossier). Question for the human: does 'unversioned at the wire' mean a fixed permanent /v1 literal with no rolling versioning, or literally no version segment in the URL — and if the latter, is that a code gap (strip /v1) or was the dossier simply wrong from the start?

sources: dossier=Net position lists the instance-scoped routes among cascade-graph's surface but never mentions a graph/edges projection (2026-05-11, artifact-only); doc=cascade-graph.md:12 (pre-fix) described only 'a family of read endpoints' with 'per-instance node state', never the graph itself; code=cascade_graph.go computeCascadeGraph builds CascadeNode entries (EdgesIn/EdgesOut derived from template subscriptions, run summary, last terminal event) and handler.go:349-353 returns it under the cascade_graph response key on the instance-read route the doc already claims to cover
note: The doc already claims ownership of the per-instance read route ('per-instance node state') but omitted the one artifact literally named 'cascade graph' — the concept's own namesake. This is a self-containment/completeness gap on a route the doc already claims, not a new intent claim requiring separate authorization. Added a sentence describing the per-instance cascade graph (nodes joined with subscription edges, run summaries, last terminal events).

sources: dossier=Net position route list (/observability/*, /events, /frames, /nodes/{instance}/{type}, /dispatches — narrower than actual code, 2026-05-11, artifact-only); design corpus=observability.md:19 Boundaries explicitly defers 'the operator-dashboard HTTP routes' to cascade-graph as a general grant, not a route-by-route enumeration; doc=cascade-graph.md:12 (pre-fix) enumerated only 5 route groups and said it 'Reads rimsky's own runtime state'; code=handler.go Routes() (lines 37-59) registers 11 route groups including /claim-producers, /executors, /templates, /instances, /lock-holders, /system/health, /system/summary, with the peer routes reading deps.Discovery (cache) not runtime tables
note: observability.md independently corroborates that cascade-graph's boundary is the operator-dashboard HTTP surface as a whole, not the narrow 5-group list the thin single-source dossier happened to enumerate — the dossier predates the peer/template/instance/lock-holder/system routes' documentation. Broadened the 'What it is' enumeration to the full route family and corrected the data-source claim to distinguish table reads from discovery-cache reads.

sources: dossier=silent on ownership wording; design corpus=observability.md:19 Boundaries 'Does NOT own: ... the operator-dashboard HTTP routes (see cascade-graph)' vs control-api.md:21 Boundaries 'Owns: ... the observability read handlers, ...'; doc=cascade-graph.md:20 (pre-fix) 'Owns: the read-route definitions, the per-route handlers, ...' with no deference sentence
note: observability.md's explicit deference to cascade-graph corroborates that cascade-graph is the intended sole owner of this handler surface, making control-api.md's overlapping 'the observability read handlers' claim the stale side (not editable here per scope — control-api.md needs a matching deference or narrowing edit in a separate change). Added an explicit sole-ownership clause to cascade-graph.md's Boundaries so a reader isn't left to resolve the overlap themselves from this side.
